items.title: EU/EEA students: register with the police (UDI) if staying more than 3 months
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE: registrazione presso la polizia (UDI) per soggiorni oltre 3 mesi

other: Nordic citizens (Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Iceland) do not need to register
Swiss citizens: listed together with EU/EEA on UiO's health-insurance page; the UDI student page checked only names EU/EEA nationals - confirm with UDI

items.summary: No visa or permit is needed, but EU/EEA nationals who will study in Norway for more than three months must register. You register an application online via UDI and then attend a police appointment (in Oslo: the SUA service centre) within 3 months of arrival; you can start studying before the appointment.
steps: Once in Oslo, register an application in the UDI online portal and choose Oslo as municipality
Book the first available appointment at Oslo Police, Servicesenteret for utenlandske arbeidstakere (SUA)
Bring passport or national ID card, EHIC or private health insurance valid for the whole stay, admission letter, a personal declaration of sufficient funds and the UDI application receipt
If staying 6 months or more, report the move to Norway to the Tax Administration at the same SUA visit (see no-registration-eu)
items.deadline: Within 3 months of arrival (UiO advises booking the first available slot even if it falls after the 3 months)
items.notes: Steps and documents come from UiO's page (official university source). Cost not stated on the pages read; secondary university pages say registration is free but this was not confirmed on a UDI page today.

items.title: Non-EU students: study permit with proof of funds
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: permesso di studio con prova dei mezzi economici

other: Admitted to a university or university college and studying full time

items.summary: Non-EU/EEA students need a study permit from UDI. You must document NOK 15,488/month or NOK 170,368/year for living costs (2026-2027), plus tuition if you have to pay it, held in a Norwegian bank account or the institution's deposit account. After arrival you book a police appointment to get the residence card.
steps: Apply to UDI after admission and pay the application fee
Document funds: NOK 170,368 for a year, or NOK 77,440 (autumn 2026) / NOK 92,928 (spring 2027) for one semester, plus tuition fees if applicable
After arrival, book a police appointment via UDI immediately; the police notify the Tax Administration
items.cost: NOK 5,400 application fee for applicants over 18 (UDI fees table; the table shows no validity date)
items.notes: The UDI page lists the amounts without naming the year; UiO's tuition page confirms NOK 170,368 is the 2026/2027 figure. The UDI page's tuition paragraph still mentions fees 'for the 2025/2026 academic year' (apparently not updated).

items.title: EU/EEA students staying 6+ months: report a move to Norway (National Registry)
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE con soggiorno di almeno 6 mesi: notifica di trasferimento all'anagrafe (Folkeregister)

other: Students staying only one semester (under 6 months) and not working do not get an ID number from the Tax Administration

items.summary: If you will stay 6 months or more, you book an appointment with the Tax Administration to report a move to Norway; if approved you receive a permanent national identity number (fødselsnummer). In Oslo, if you booked the police appointment at SUA, you are passed to the Tax Administration after it.
steps: Book a Tax Administration appointment, or use the SUA police appointment in Oslo
Bring your rental agreement, the completed form RF-1401 'Notification of a move to Norway' and the documents for the police appointment
UiO: students enrolled for 2 semesters or more can book the Tax Administration appointment at SUA without a police appointment

items.title: Non-EU students: registration happens through the police appointment
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: la registrazione avviene tramite l'appuntamento con la polizia
items.summary: Non-EU/EEA students do not need a separate Tax Administration appointment: the police notify the Tax Administration after your residence-card appointment. With a study permit of more than 9 months you are registered as resident and get a national identity number; otherwise the letter explains next steps (often a D number).
items.deadline: Book the police appointment via UDI immediately after arrival

items.title: National identity number vs D number
items.summary: Norway has two ID numbers: the permanent national identity number (for people with a right of residence staying 6 months or more) and the temporary D number. You cannot apply for a D number yourself; an authority or enterprise (e.g. the Tax Administration for people liable to tax, Nav, banks) requests it. A D number becomes 'inactive' 5 years after it was assigned.
items.notes: Ny i Norge adds that if you have no ID number, the Tax Administration issues a D number when you apply for a tax deduction card.

items.title: Tax deduction card needed before you work
items.title_it: Tax deduction card (skattekort) necessaria prima di lavorare

other: Only for students who work (non-EU: only if the permit allows work)

items.summary: Any student who works in Norway must have a tax deduction card. With a Norwegian ID number you apply online; without one you book an appointment with the Tax Administration (an ID check). A European eID (eIDAS) cannot be used to apply.

items.title: EU/EEA/Swiss students: bring your EHIC (or private insurance)
items.title_it: Studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri: porta la tessera TEAM (EHIC) o un'assicurazione privata
items.summary: Students are in principle not considered resident in Norway, so EU/EEA/Swiss students use their home-country EHIC for necessary care, paying the same co-payment as Norwegian patients; without a valid EHIC you pay the full cost. EHIC or private insurance valid for the whole stay is also needed for the police registration. Private travel insurance is recommended on top.

items.title: Working in Norway makes you a compulsory member of the National Insurance Scheme
items.title_it: Lavorare in Norvegia comporta l'iscrizione obbligatoria alla previdenza nazionale (folketrygden)

applies_to.min_work_hours: any employment with a Norwegian employer (no minimum stated)

items.summary: Under Nav's rules, non-residents who work in Norway are compulsory members of the National Insurance Scheme (folketrygden); the employer must be liable for the Norwegian employer's contribution. Helsenorge tells students who take a job to check with Nav how it affects their rights.
items.notes: The Nav page does not say explicitly from which day membership starts for workers, nor how it interacts with the EHIC for part-time student jobs; a human should confirm with Nav.

items.title: Non-EU students: National Insurance membership depends on length of stay
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: l'iscrizione alla previdenza nazionale dipende dalla durata del soggiorno
items.summary: Under 3 months: no membership, you need private or home-country cover. 3-12 months: you can apply to Nav for voluntary membership (processing can take months, so insure yourself meanwhile). Over 12 months: membership is automatic once you are registered as resident in the National Registry.
steps: 3-12 months: send Nav's voluntary-membership form with admission letter, passport, residence card and ID/D number to the Nav office of your municipality
items.notes: Synthesis from UiO's page; Nav's own foreign-students page returned 404 today.

items.title: Bank account: you need a Norwegian ID number (national ID or D number)
items.title_it: Conto bancario: serve un numero d'identità norvegese (fødselsnummer o D-number)
items.summary: To open a bank account in Norway you must be resident, show valid ID (passport or national ID card) and have a Norwegian identity number, either a national identity number or a D number. If you have neither, the Tax Administration issues a D number when you apply for a tax deduction card.
items.authority: Ny i Norge (Norwegian government portal for newcomers)
items.notes: Individual banks' requirements were not checked. Non-EU students must keep their documented funds in a Norwegian bank account or the institution's deposit account (UDI).

items.title: Ruter student 30-day ticket (Oslo and Akershus)
items.title_it: Abbonamento studenti Ruter da 30 giorni (Oslo e Akershus)

other: Full-time student at an institution that qualifies for Lånekassen support
Course of at least 3 months and at least 30 credits per term (part-time and 'visiting' students excluded)
Must carry valid student ID for the current term

items.summary: Ruter gives a 40% discount on the 30-day ticket (only that ticket) to full-time students under 30. Buy it in the Ruter app (Period ticket > 30-day > student). Price: see the Oslo city file.
items.deadline: Must be activated at the latest the day before you turn 30
items.cost: NOK 393 per 30 days, zone 1 (price list from 1 August 2026)

interpretations.hypothesis: Ruter's page says 'Norwegian student'; read as enrolled full-time at a Norwegian institution, so foreign degree and full-time exchange students (30 credits/term) qualify.

The price list footnote says 'Fulltime students 20-29 years old qualifying for support from Lånekassen', which could be read as requiring personal Lånekassen eligibility (most foreign students are not eligible).

items.notes: Ruter's page lists 'visiting students' among those excluded; whether that covers exchange students is not defined. Vy reported on 28 Oct 2026 that the student ticket became NOK 100 cheaper from 1 Nov 2026 - see Oslo city file.

items.title: EU/EEA students can work without a permit
items.title_it: Gli studenti UE/SEE possono lavorare senza permesso
items.summary: EU/EEA students need no work permit and can work and study from day one, with no hour limit stated. They must still register with the police within 3 months and get a tax deduction card.

items.title: Non-EU students: up to 20 hours/week in term, full time in holidays
items.title_it: Studenti extra-UE: fino a 20 ore/settimana durante i corsi, a tempo pieno nelle vacanze
items.summary: A granted study permit automatically allows part-time work up to 20 hours per week (remote work included) and full-time work in holidays. Self-employment or running your own business is not allowed.

interpretations.hypothesis: UDI: the right to work 20 h/week follows automatically from the study permit, with no further condition stated.
UiO: 20 h/week applies 'during your first year of study'; the work permission is not renewed automatically and you must document satisfactory study progress to keep working.

items.title: No general statutory minimum wage; sector minimums only
items.title_it: Nessun salario minimo legale generale; minimi solo in alcuni settori
items.summary: Norway has no general statutory minimum wage. Legal minimum rates apply in ten sectors through generally applicable collective agreements, e.g. from 6 Nov 2026: hospitality NOK 215.29/h (over 20, or 18+ after 4 months; lower rates at 17-18), cleaning NOK 247.29/h (18+), construction unskilled NOK 250.63/h.
items.notes: Youth rates: hospitality under 17 NOK 153.08, 17 NOK 162.58, 18 NOK 176.84; cleaning under 18 NOK 196.05. Other sectors: automotive, electricians, fish processing, road freight, agriculture, tour buses, maritime construction.

items.title: Tuition fees for non-EU/EEA/Swiss students (since 2023)

other: Exchange students from partner universities are not affected
Exemptions based on residence or close ties to Norway

items.summary: At the University of Oslo, citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland pay tuition fees unless exempt; students admitted before 2023 are not affected. EU/EEA and Swiss students pay no tuition, only the semester fee. 2026/2027 master's fees at UiO range from NOK 136,000 to NOK 295,000 per year.
items.deadline: Payment due two weeks after the invoice is issued; full year in advance (second-year students may pay per semester)
items.cost: NOK 136,000-295,000 per year for UiO master's programmes (2026/2027)
items.notes: National legal basis (government page) not opened today because the search budget ran out; the UiO page is the source. Other Norwegian institutions set their own amounts.
